title: Stop Butter Basting Meat, Do This Instead | Techniquely with Lan Lam

locations.name: America's Test Kitchen Test Kitchen
locations.basis: explicit mention of the Test Kitchen in transcript

summary: Lan Lam reframes butter basting as not universally required for home cooking and walks through practical, timing-conscious alternatives across proteins. The video contrasts traditional basting with more efficient methods, using steak as the primary example, and then extends the approach to pan sauces for chicken and flaky fish. By focusing on heat management, browning, and building flavor through fond-based sauces (instead of relying on continuous basting), the episode demonstrates how to achieve sear, depth of flavor, and moisture with minimal fuss. The demonstrations—steak without aggressive basting, a brown-butter finish, skillet-roasted chicken, and Steve Dunn’s fish-baste method—are tied together with guidance on when baste is advantageous (notably for delicate fish) and when it’s safer to skip it while still delivering a robust, flavorful result.
